## 1. Design model and assumptions

- All section properties are used in mm and N units.
- \(L_{ex}=L_{ey}=L_{ez}=3000\ \text{mm}\).
- \(A_{\text{eff}}=A\); local and distortional buckling reductions are therefore not applied.
- The centroidal axial load introduces no design bending moment.
- Because each channel is singly symmetric about the \(x\)-axis:
  - strong-axis flexural buckling, \(N_{cr,x}\), is uncoupled;
  - minor-axis flexure and torsion are coupled, giving torsional-flexural buckling, \(N_{cr,TF}\).
- The ends are twist-restrained but free to warp, so the warping term uses the full \(3.0\ \text{m}\) torsional length.
- Since \(L_{ez}=3.0\ \text{m}>2.50\ \text{m}\), the maker knock-down factor is
  \[
  k_{VM}=0.92.
  \]
- Buckling curve b is used for every mode:
  \[
  \alpha=0.34,\qquad \gamma_{M1}=1.00.
  \]

The common flexural coefficient is

\[
\frac{\pi^2E}{L^2}
=
\frac{\pi^2(210000)}{3000^2}
=
0.230290769.
\]

## 2. Elastic buckling equations

The minor-axis and polar radii of gyration are

\[
r_y^2=\frac{I_y}{A},
\]

\[
r_0^2=r_x^2+r_y^2+x_0^2+y_0^2
=\frac{I_x+I_y}{A}+x_0^2,
\]

because \(y_0=0\).

The uncoupled elastic critical loads are

\[
N_{cr,x}=\frac{\pi^2EI_x}{L_{ex}^2},
\qquad
N_{cr,y}=\frac{\pi^2EI_y}{L_{ey}^2},
\]

\[
N_{cr,T}
=
\frac{1}{r_0^2}
\left(
GJ+\frac{\pi^2EI_w}{L_{ez}^2}
\right).
\]

For a section singly symmetric about \(x\), the lower torsional-flexural root is

\[
N_{cr,TF}
=
\frac{
N_{cr,y}+N_{cr,T}
-\sqrt{
\left(N_{cr,y}-N_{cr,T}\right)^2
+4\left(\frac{x_0}{r_0}\right)^2N_{cr,y}N_{cr,T}
}
}{
2\left[1-\left(\frac{x_0}{r_0}\right)^2\right]
}.
\]

The maker-rule slenderness is based on

\[
N_{cr}=\min(N_{cr,x},N_{cr,y},N_{cr,TF}).
\]

## 3. Section-by-section calculation

### Geometric quantities

| Section | \(A\) (mm²) | \(r_y^2\) (mm²) | \(r_y\) (mm) | \(r_0^2\) (mm²) | \(r_0\) (mm) | \((x_0/r_0)^2\) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| VM-C140 | 620 | 935.4839 | 30.5857 | 5844.6452 | 76.4503 | 0.3018147 |
| VM-C160 | 800 | 1153.7500 | 33.9669 | 7554.7500 | 86.9181 | 0.3178133 |
| VM-C180 | 1080 | 1500.0000 | 38.7298 | 9615.4563 | 98.0584 | 0.3191903 |
| VM-C200 | 1350 | 1780.7407 | 42.1988 | 11698.8148 | 108.1611 | 0.3285803 |

### Elastic critical loads

Here,

\[
B=GJ+\frac{\pi^2EI_w}{L^2},
\qquad
N_{cr,T}=\frac{B}{r_0^2}.
\]

| Section | \(N_{cr,x}\) (kN) | \(N_{cr,y}\) (kN) | \(B\) (\(10^6\ \text{N mm}^2\)) | \(N_{cr,T}\) (kN) | \(N_{cr,TF}\) (kN) | Governing mode |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| VM-C140 | 449.067 | 133.569 | 604.537846 | 103.434 | 74.756 | Torsional-flexural |
| VM-C160 | 736.930 | 212.558 | 1306.968078 | 173.000 | 121.490 | Torsional-flexural |
| VM-C180 | 1255.085 | 373.071 | 3318.715386 | 345.144 | 228.986 | Torsional-flexural |
| VM-C200 | 1888.384 | 553.619 | 6927.786927 | 592.179 | 363.591 | Torsional-flexural |

Thus, for every section,

\[
N_{cr}=N_{cr,TF}.
\]

## 4. Eurocode resistance and maker-rule checks

The slenderness, reduction factor, and resistance are

\[
\bar{\lambda}=\sqrt{\frac{Af_y}{N_{cr}}},
\]

\[
\Phi=
\frac12\left[
1+\alpha(\bar{\lambda}-0.2)+\bar{\lambda}^2
\right],
\]

\[
\chi=
\frac{1}{
\Phi+\sqrt{\Phi^2-\bar{\lambda}^2}
},
\]

\[
N_{b,Rd}
=
k_{VM}\frac{\chi Af_y}{\gamma_{M1}}.
\]

| Section | \(Af_y\) (kN) | \(\bar{\lambda}\) | \(\Phi\) | \(\chi\) | \(N_{b,Rd}\) (kN) | \(N_{Ed}/N_{b,Rd}\) | Check |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| VM-C140 | 220.10 | 1.715882 | 2.229826 | 0.273683 | 55.419 | 2.075 | Fails resistance and \(\bar{\lambda}\le1.30\) |
| VM-C160 | 284.00 | 1.528934 | 1.894738 | 0.331802 | 86.693 | 1.327 | Fails resistance and \(\bar{\lambda}\le1.30\) |
| VM-C180 | 383.40 | 1.293962 | 1.523143 | 0.429802 | 151.603 | 0.7586 | Passes |
| VM-C200 | 479.25 | 1.148086 | 1.320225 | 0.507083 | 223.578 | 0.5144 | Passes, but heavier |

Because all sections have the same steel density and strut length, mass is proportional to gross area. Therefore, VM-C180 is lighter than the other passing section, VM-C200.

## 5. Detailed check of the selected VM-C180

### Radii of gyration

\[
r_y=\sqrt{\frac{1.620\times10^6}{1080}}
=\sqrt{1500}
=38.7298\ \text{mm},
\]

\[
r_0^2
=
\frac{(5.450+1.620)\times10^6}{1080}+55.4^2
\]

\[
=6546.2963+3069.1600
=9615.4563\ \text{mm}^2,
\]

\[
r_0=98.0584\ \text{mm}.
\]

### Elastic critical loads

\[
N_{cr,x}
=
\frac{\pi^2(210000)(5.450\times10^6)}{3000^2}
=1255.085\ \text{kN},
\]

\[
N_{cr,y}
=
\frac{\pi^2(210000)(1.620\times10^6)}{3000^2}
=373.071\ \text{kN}.
\]

For torsion,

\[
GJ=81000(2590)=209.790\times10^6\ \text{N mm}^2,
\]

\[
\frac{\pi^2EI_w}{L^2}
=
0.230290769(13.50\times10^9)
=3108.925\times10^6\ \text{N mm}^2,
\]

\[
N_{cr,T}
=
\frac{209.790\times10^6+3108.925\times10^6}
{9615.4563}
=345.144\ \text{kN}.
\]

The coupling parameter is

\[
\left(\frac{x_0}{r_0}\right)^2
=
\frac{55.4^2}{9615.4563}
=0.3191903.
\]

Hence

\[
N_{cr,TF}
=
\frac{
373.071+345.144
-\sqrt{
(373.071-345.144)^2
+4(0.3191903)(373.071)(345.144)
}
}{
2(1-0.3191903)
}
\]

\[
=
\frac{718.214874-406.423089}{1.361619479}
=228.986\ \text{kN}.
\]

Therefore,

\[
N_{cr}=\min(1255.085,\ 373.071,\ 228.986)
=228.986\ \text{kN}.
\]

### Slenderness and resistance

\[
\bar{\lambda}
=
\sqrt{\frac{1080(355)}{228986}}
=
\sqrt{1.674338}
=1.293962
<1.30.
\]

\[
\Phi
=
\frac12\left[
1+0.34(1.293962-0.2)+1.293962^2
\right]
=1.523143.
\]

\[
\chi
=
\frac{1}{
1.523143+
\sqrt{1.523143^2-1.293962^2}
}
=0.429802.
\]

\[
N_{b,Rd}
=
0.92(0.429802)(1080)(355)
=151603\ \text{N}
=151.603\ \text{kN}.
\]

\[
\text{Utilization}
=
\frac{115}{151.603}
=0.75856.
\]

## Final conclusion

The lightest compliant section is **VM-C180**. Its governing mode is torsional-flexural buckling. It satisfies both the maker slenderness limit and the factored load requirement:

\[
\bar{\lambda}=1.293962<1.30,
\qquad
N_{b,Rd}=151.603\ \text{kN}>N_{Ed}=115\ \text{kN}.
\]

| chi | 0.429802 |

| Utilization | 0.75856 (75.86%) |

## Assumptions and calculation basis

- The Darcy–Weisbach equation is used, with the Darcy friction factor from the Colebrook equation.
- Tank and reactor liquid-surface velocities are negligible.
- The stated \(22.0\text{ m}\) is the total supply-surface-to-reactor-surface static head. The pump centerline elevation of \(3.20\text{ m}\) is therefore used only in the NPSH calculation, not added again to \(H_{sys}\).
- \(\Sigma K_{total}=14.0\) includes the suction minor losses; \(\Sigma K_s=2.8\) is the suction-only portion used for NPSH.
- A trim is acceptable only if \(H_{pump}(90,D_{trim})\ge H_{sys}\), with integer diameters rounded upward.

## 1. Pipe velocity, Reynolds number, and friction factor

Pipe area:

\[
A=\frac{\pi D_{pipe}^2}{4}
=\frac{\pi(0.1023)^2}{4}
=0.0082194195\ \text{m}^2
\]

Velocity:

\[
v=\frac{Q}{A}
=\frac{0.0250}{0.0082194195}
=3.041577\ \text{m/s}
\]

Velocity head:

\[
\frac{v^2}{2g}
=\frac{(3.041577)^2}{2(9.81)}
=0.4715185\ \text{m}
\]

Reynolds number:

\[
Re=\frac{vD_{pipe}}{\nu}
=\frac{(3.041577)(0.1023)}{1.2\times10^{-6}}
=2.59294\times10^5
\]

Relative roughness:

\[
\frac{\varepsilon}{D_{pipe}}
=\frac{0.000045}{0.1023}
=4.39883\times10^{-4}
\]

Solving the Colebrook equation,

\[
\frac{1}{\sqrt f}
=
-2\log_{10}\left(
\frac{\varepsilon/D}{3.7}
+\frac{2.51}{Re\sqrt f}
\right)
\]

gives

\[
\boxed{f_D=0.0180733}
\]

## 2. System head at \(90.0\text{ m}^3/\text{h}\)

The reactor-to-supply pressure difference is

\[
\Delta p=185.0-101.3=83.7\text{ kPa}=83700\text{ Pa}
\]

and

\[
\rho g=(1150)(9.81)=11281.5\ \text{Pa/m}
\]

Thus the pressure head is

\[
\frac{\Delta p}{\rho g}
=\frac{83700}{11281.5}
=7.419226\ \text{m}
\]

Total pipe resistance coefficient:

\[
f_D\frac{L_{total}}{D_{pipe}}+\Sigma K_{total}
=
0.0180733\left(\frac{85.0}{0.1023}\right)+14.0
\]

\[
=0.0180733(830.88954)+14.0
=15.016933+14.0
=29.016933
\]

Total friction and minor loss:

\[
h_{L,total}
=29.016933(0.4715185)
=13.682020\ \text{m}
\]

Therefore,

\[
H_{sys}
=
\Delta z_{total}
+\frac{p_{reactor}-p_{atm}}{\rho g}
+h_{L,total}
\]

\[
H_{sys}
=22.0+7.419226+13.682020
=\boxed{43.101246\ \text{m}}
\]

## 3. Available NPSH

Suction resistance coefficient:

\[
f_D\frac{L_s}{D_{pipe}}+\Sigma K_s
=
0.0180733\left(\frac{6.0}{0.1023}\right)+2.8
\]

\[
=0.0180733(58.651026)+2.8
=1.060019+2.8
=3.860019
\]

Suction-line loss:

\[
h_{L,s}=3.860019(0.4715185)=1.820070\ \text{m}
\]

Because the pump centerline is \(3.20\text{ m}\) above the supply-tank liquid surface,

\[
NPSH_A
=
\frac{p_{atm}-p_v}{\rho g}
-z_s-h_{L,s}
\]

\[
\frac{p_{atm}-p_v}{\rho g}
=
\frac{101300-18000}{11281.5}
=7.383770\ \text{m}
\]

\[
NPSH_A
=7.383770-3.20-1.820070
=\boxed{2.363700\ \text{m}}
\]

The cavitation rule requires

\[
NPSH_A\ge1.15NPSH_{R,corr}+0.50
\]

so the maximum permissible corrected required NPSH is

\[
NPSH_{R,corr}
\le
\frac{2.363700-0.50}{1.15}
=\boxed{1.620608\ \text{m}}
\]

## 4. Model screening

Let

\[
r=\frac{D_{trim}}{D_0}
\]

At \(Q=90\text{ m}^3/\text{h}\), the head requirement gives

\[
r\ge
\sqrt{\frac{H_{sys}+S_0(90)^2}{H_0}}
\]

The POR requires

\[
\frac{90}{1.15Q_{BEP0}}
\le r\le
\frac{90}{0.70Q_{BEP0}}
\]

and cavitation requires

\[
r\ge
\left(\frac{NPSH_{R0}}{1.620608}\right)^{2/3}
\]

The resulting integer-diameter constraints are:

| Model | Head minimum \(D\) (mm) | POR integer range (mm) | Cavitation minimum \(D\) (mm) | Absolute trim minimum (mm) | Governing minimum |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| KV-100-200 | 218, above \(D_0=208\) | 177–208 | 185 | 177 | Infeasible |
| KV-80-250 | 228 | 231–250 | 236 | 213 | 236 |
| KV-100-250 | 228 | 196–250 | 211 | 213 | 228 |
| KV-125-250 | 219 | 151–247 | 199 | 213 | 219 |

KV-100-200 is rejected because even at full diameter,

\[
H_{pump}=46.5-0.00095(90)^2
=46.5-7.695
=38.805\text{ m}
<43.101\text{ m}
\]

### Performance of the remaining candidates

For KV-80-250 at \(D=236\text{ mm}\), \(r=0.944\):

\[
H_{pump}=64(0.944)^2-0.00120(90)^2
=47.312704\text{ m}
\]

\[
\eta
=0.745-0.00015[90-85(0.944)]^2-0.25(1-0.944)
=0.716711
\]

\[
P_{shaft}
=
\frac{\rho gQH_{pump}}{\eta}
=
\frac{0.2820375(47.312704)}{0.716711}
=18.618\text{ kW}
\]

but

\[
P_{motor,derated}=0.88(18.5)=16.280\text{ kW}
\]

so KV-80-250 fails the motor rule. Checking the feasible trims \(236\) through \(250\text{ mm}\), the minimum shaft power occurs at \(236\text{ mm}\), so no larger trim rescues this model.

For the two passing models:

| Model | \(D_{trim}\) (mm) | \(H_{pump}\) (m) | \(\eta_{pump}\) | \(NPSH_{R,corr}\) (m) | \(P_{shaft}\) (kW) | \(P_{motor,derated}\) (kW) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| KV-100-250 | 228 | 43.468128 | 0.757856 | 1.435218 | 16.1767 | 19.360 |
| KV-125-250 | 219 | 43.399440 | 0.713380 | 1.402625 | 17.1581 | 26.400 |

Thus KV-100-250 is selected because it has the lower shaft power.

## 5. Final verification of the selected pump

For KV-100-250 at \(D_{trim}=228\text{ mm}\),

\[
r=\frac{228}{250}=0.912
\]

Pump head:

\[
H_{pump}
=62(0.912)^2-0.00100(90)^2
=43.468128\text{ m}
\]

The next smaller integer trim would be \(227\text{ mm}\):

\[
H_{pump}(227)
=62\left(\frac{227}{250}\right)^2-8.1
=43.016768\text{ m}
<43.101246\text{ m}
\]

so \(228\text{ mm}\) is the minimum acceptable integer diameter.

BEP and POR:

\[
Q_{BEP,trim}=100(0.912)=91.2\text{ m}^3/\text{h}
\]

\[
POR=[0.70(91.2),1.15(91.2)]
=[63.84,104.88]\text{ m}^3/\text{h}
\]

and \(90.0\text{ m}^3/\text{h}\) is within this range.

Efficiency:

\[
\eta_{pump}
=
0.780
-0.00010(90-91.2)^2
-0.25(1-0.912)
\]

\[
\eta_{pump}
=0.780-0.000144-0.022
=\boxed{0.757856}
\]

Corrected required NPSH:

\[
NPSH_{R,corr}
=
1.25\left(\frac{250}{228}\right)^{1.5}
=\boxed{1.435218\text{ m}}
\]

Cavitation-rule requirement:

\[
1.15NPSH_{R,corr}+0.50
=1.15(1.435218)+0.50
=2.150500\text{ m}
\]

\[
NPSH_A=2.363700\text{ m}>2.150500\text{ m}
\]

Shaft power:

\[
P_{shaft}
=
\frac{(1150)(9.81)(0.0250)(43.468128)}{0.757856}
=16.1767\text{ kW}
\]

Derated motor power:

\[
P_{motor,derated}=0.88(22.0)=19.360\text{ kW}
\]

Therefore, the selected pump is **KV-100-250 with a \(228\text{ mm}\) trimmed impeller**.
